methodology: The study utilized enzyme-assisted oxygen tolerance nitroxide-mediated miniemulsion polymerization (NMP) with alkoxyamine Dispolreg 007 as the initiator, demonstrating that the process can be carried out under aerobic conditions without degassing treatment.
research_objective: To achieve and demonstrate the first case of oxygen tolerance nitroxide-mediated miniemulsion polymerization using enzyme-assisted systems.

key_findings.finding: Enzyme-assisted oxygen tolerance nitroxide-mediated miniemulsion polymerization (NMP) was successfully achieved.
The polymerization can be performed under aerobic conditions without degassing treatment, providing new opportunities for NMP in preparation of polymeric nano-objects.
Development of RDRP techniques for oxygen tolerance NMP miniemulsion polymerization, with Dispolreg 007 as the initiator and BMA or BzMA as monomers
Enzyme-assisted NMP miniemulsion polymerization can achieve oxygen-free conditions, improving the oxygen tolerance of the system.
Dispolreg 007 cannot consume large amounts of oxygen under open to air condition similar to NMP solution systems.
Enzyme-assisted oxygen tolerance in NMP miniemulsion polymerization

In compared with other RDRP methods, NMP was highlighted by the clean and low toxic product which is favorable for some sensitive biological and electronic applications. Here we reported the first case of oxygen tolerance nitroxide-mediated miniemulsion polymerization, by introducing glucose oxidase (GOx) and ascorbic acid (AsAc) to the system. Without degassing treatment, the miniemulsion polymerization can be carried on using alkoxyamine 3-(((2-cyanopropan-2- yl)oxy) (cyclohexyl)amino)-2,2-dimethyl-3-phenylpropanenitrile (Dispolreg 007) as the initiator. The oxygen tolerance NMP miniemulsion exhibited similar living and control behavior to the degassing system, and the chain extension could also be performed without degassing. The characteristics of this enzyme assisted oxygen tolerant heterogeneous NMP may provide exciting new opportunities for increased versatility of NMP polymerization in preparation of polymeric nano-objects. 1.
